name: Prone Incline Cobra Raise
description: The prone incline cobra raise is performed lying face-down on a low-incline bench (15-30 degrees), raising the arms overhead while simultaneously extending the thoracic spine and externally rotating the shoulders — forming a 'cobra' posture. It trains the lower trapezius, thoracic extensors, and posterior rotator cuff through a full range of controlled spinal and shoulder movement, commonly used in posture correction and shoulder rehabilitation protocols.

execution.starting_position: Lie prone on a low-incline bench (15-30 degrees). Arms hang down in front of the bench, thumbs facing up.
execution.setup_instructions: No load is needed initially — this is a bodyweight or very light dumbbell movement. Use a bench inclined just enough to allow the arms to hang freely.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms hanging, thumbs up.
Step 2: Simultaneously raise the arms overhead while extending the thoracic spine.
Step 3: At peak, externally rotate so thumbs point behind — 'cobra' position.
Step 5: Lower under control, returning to the starting hang.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise and extension. Inhale returning.
common_mistakes: Extending from the lumbar spine rather than the thoracic spine
Not fully externally rotating the shoulders at the top
safety_considerations: Very light loads or bodyweight only — this is a postural and rehabilitative exercise
Avoid if experiencing thoracic or shoulder pain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms hanging to full overhead position with thoracic extension and external rotation.
coaching_cues: Lead with the chest — extend the thoracic spine, not the lumbar
Thumbs point to the ceiling at the top, then point behind you
Squeeze the shoulder blades together and down
